harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a minimal inventory application (JSON inventory served via a Python http.server) on node1, running as an enabled systemd service (inventory-app.service) bound to 0.0.0.0:8181, verified reachable via $NODE_IP:8181, while AppArmor (the system's mandatory access control) remained continuously enforcing (13/13 profiles enforce, module loaded). Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot id and service/MAC health, issued `shutdown -r now`, polled until exec access returned, confirmed the boot id changed (e4e401d2... -> 5e5b6798...), and verified post-restart that the service, port 8181 listener, inventory data, and AppArmor enforce mode all recovered.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1: Ubuntu 16.04, confirmed AppArmor as the MAC system (no SELinux), no pre-existing inventory app
Created /opt/inventory-app/inventory.json and server.py (Python 3.5-compatible http.server) serving inventory data on 0.0.0.0:8181
Created and enabled systemd unit inventory-app.service; fixed a Python 3.5 compatibility bug (TCPServer context-manager support added in 3.6) and got the service active
Verified port 8181 listening, curl via $NODE_IP:8181 returns inventory JSON, and AppArmor stayed in enforcing mode (13/13 profiles enforce) throughout setup
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline (service active/enabled, AppArmor enforcing, curl success)
Issued a backgrounded `shutdown -r now` so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned; confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart recovery: service active/enabled, port 8181 listening, curl returns inventory JSON, AppArmor still enforcing 13/13 profiles

evidence.requirement: Inventory application served over TCP port 8181 on node1
evidence.summary: ss shows python3 listening on *:8181 and curl to $NODE_IP:8181 returns the inventory JSON payload

evidence.requirement: Mandatory access control (AppArmor) remains in enforcing mode while the app is set up and serving
evidence.summary: aa-status confirms apparmor module loaded with 13/13 profiles in enforce mode, checked before app creation, immediately after service start, and just before restart
Captured boot_id e4e401d2-3dd8-48c6-848a-545631b9e229, service active+enabled, AppArmor enforcing, port 8181 listening, curl success

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Backgrounded shutdown -r now returned immediately; subsequent exec failed with connection refused (node down); later exec succeeded with new boot_id 5e5b6798-8668-4820-991f-04ac8af4be76, proving a real reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of inventory app, port 8181, and MAC enforcing state
evidence.summary: Post-restart: apparmor still 13/13 enforce, inventory-app.service active/enabled, port 8181 listening, curl via $NODE_IP returns inventory JSON
